2027-07-12.title: Monday of the eighth week after Pentecost
readings: Paul's ministry was a burden to no one; beware of those who disguise themselves as apostles of Christ
“Follow me, and I will make you fish for people”: the first four disciples leave their nets
2027-07-12.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Eighth Sunday after Pentecost. No commemoration of its own is printed in the Panchangam today. St Benedict, the monk of Italy, is printed with the Sunday of 11 July, the day before.
2027-07-12.verse: And he said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.”
theo: Today's Epistle comes from the most painful pages of St Paul's letters, where he has to defend his own ministry before the people he had loved and served. Rival preachers had come to Corinth, boasting of their gifts, and some of them were being paid for their teaching. They looked down on Paul because he had worked with his hands (Acts 18:3) and had asked nothing from the Corinthians. Paul answers with a sharp irony: “Did I commit a sin by humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I proclaimed God's good news to you without payment?” He had accepted help from other churches, “I robbed other churches by accepting support from them in order to serve you,” and he lists the friends from Macedonia who supplied his needs, the Philippians who had always helped him (Philippians 4:15–16). So, he says, “I did not burden anyone,” and “I will continue to refrain from burdening you in any way.” We must read him rightly. Paul does not teach that the Church should never support her ministers; elsewhere he says plainly that the Lord commanded those who proclaim the gospel to get their living by the gospel (1 Corinthians 9:14). He is saying that he gave up this right at Corinth so that no one could say he preached for money. And he ends with the reason of the heart: “And why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!”

Then Paul's tone turns grave: “For such boasters are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ. And no wonder! Even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light. So it is not strange if his ministers also disguise themselves as ministers of righteousness. Their end will match their deeds.” The danger he names is not crude evil but a polished counterfeit, a message that sounds beautiful and a preacher who looks holy, but who seeks his own glory or gain. How does a simple believer tell the difference? The Lord himself gave the test: “You will know them by their fruits” (Matthew 7:16). St John adds: “do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God” (1 John 4:1). The Church has always taught us to ask whether a teaching agrees with the faith handed down from the Apostles, which the bishops, in communion with the successor of Peter, are charged to guard, and whether the preacher bears the fruit of humility, love and service. This is not a call to suspicion of others; it is a call to be wise, for the simple believe everything, but the clever consider their steps (Proverbs 14:15). Paul himself is the pattern of the true apostle: he gives, he does not take; he works, he does not boast.

The Gospel shows us what the true call looks like at its beginning. “As he walked by the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen. And he said to them, ‘Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.’ Immediately they left their nets and followed him.” Then two more: “James son of Zebedee and his brother John, in the boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets, and he called them. Immediately they left the boat and their father, and followed him.” These men had no theology degree, no fine speech, no fame. They had boats, nets and a father, and they had a call. Anyone who has watched the fishermen of Kerala mend their nets on the beach after the monsoon knows how much a net means to a family. They left what they had in order to follow him, and he promised them no income, only a new kind of work: to draw people toward God. The false apostles take; the true Apostles leave. Yesterday the Panchangam remembered St Benedict, the monk of Italy who began his Rule with the single word “Listen” and taught his monks to put nothing before the love of Christ (Rule, Prologue and chapter 4, in substance). He too heard “Follow me” and left what he had. The same call goes out to each of us today, in the plain places where we work and mend our nets.
outline: Ask: what is my net, the thing I would find hardest to leave if Jesus said, “Follow me”?
Four ordinary fishermen leave nets and boat at once; the call and the promise.
Point 2 · A burden to no one
Paul gives up his right to support at Corinth; his boast is love, not gain.
Even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light; test the spirits and know them by their fruits.
“Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.”
live: Name one thing you hold on to that keeps you from following Jesus more closely, and place it at his feet in prayer today.
Do one piece of service this week for which you ask nothing, and tell no one about it.
When a preacher, a message or a video claims to speak for God, ask whether it agrees with the Church's faith and bears the fruit of love and humility; ask your parish priest if you are unsure.
2027-07-12.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you walked beside the Sea of Galilee and called fishermen to follow you, and they left their nets at once. Call us also, and give us hearts that can leave what holds us back. Make us servants like Paul, a burden to no one, glad to give and not to take. Keep us from the disguises of light and from every preaching that seeks its own glory, and keep your Church in the faith of the Apostles. By the prayers of St Benedict and all your holy servants, teach us to listen and to put nothing before your love. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the Lord still calls: Follow me. We leave our place in the pew, bring bread and wine, and he gives himself for us; the One who asked nothing of the Apostles but their nets, gives us his whole self.

quick: Paul gave up his right to be supported at Corinth so that no one could say he preached for money; his boast was love.
Even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light: test the spirits and know them by their fruits.
Jesus calls four fishermen, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people,” and at once they leave their nets.
2027-07-12.action: Do one good deed today for which you ask nothing in return, and tell nobody.
2027-07-12.question: What is my net, and am I ready to leave it if Jesus calls?

family.explain: Four fishermen were mending their nets when Jesus walked by and said, “Follow me.” They left their nets and boats at once and went with him to learn how to help people come close to God. Jesus also calls us, in our family, in school and in work. St Paul teaches us to serve gladly without asking for anything. He also tells us to be wise and ask: does this teaching agree with what the Church teaches?
family.intention: We pray for fishermen and their families, especially in the monsoon when the sea is rough, and for those who are called to serve the Church.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one small thing we can leave behind to follow Jesus more closely this week?”

illus: In a fishing village near Vizhinjam a young man became a priest. His mother, who had mended nets all her life, could not read well and did not understand the long ceremony. At the end of his first Qurbono, she walked up to the altar with a small piece of old net folded in her hands. She laid it by the chalice and said quietly: I mended nets for my sons all my life. Today I give a net back to the Lord. The people who saw her said later that the sermon had come at the end, and it had been the shortest and the best of the day.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you called fishermen to follow you and promised to make them fishers of people. Call us also, and make us ready to leave what holds us. Amen.
share: Immediately they left their nets and followed him (Matthew 4:20). What do I find hardest to leave for Jesus?
I did not burden anyone (2 Corinthians 11:9). How can I serve without asking for something in return?
Even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:14). How do I test what I hear about God?
pm.resp: Lord, make us ready to follow you.
interc: For the Church and her pastors, that they may serve without seeking their own gain and be faithful to the faith of the Apostles.
For vocations to the priesthood and religious life, that many young people may hear Jesus say, “Follow me.”
For fishermen and their families, and for all who work on the sea in this monsoon season.
For those misled by false teaching, that they may find the truth and the peace of Christ.
For our parish, that we may be generous in giving and quick to follow.
pm.close: Father, you call us by name through your Son. Give us the courage of the first disciples, the generosity of Paul and the wisdom to know your voice, that we may follow you always. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the Gospel today takes us to the shore of the lake. Jesus is walking, and he sees two brothers casting a net, and he says: Follow me, and I will make you fish for people (Matthew 4:19). They were not scholars or leaders. They were working people. And the Gospel says: Immediately they left their nets and followed him (Matthew 4:20). Then it happens again with James and John, who were mending their nets in the boat with their father.

Think of what they left: the boat, the nets, the income, the father who needed them. They could not see where this would lead. They only knew who was calling. And that is the heart of every vocation: not a clear plan, but a clear voice. Jesus calls each of us in the middle of our ordinary work. The question is what we are ready to leave behind: a habit, a grudge, a fear, the love of money.

In the Epistle, St Paul shows us what it is to follow Jesus to the end. He worked with his own hands and asked nothing from the Corinthians so that nobody could say he preached for gain (2 Corinthians 11:9). He serves, he does not take. But he warns us as well: Even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:14). Not everything that shines is of God. The Lord gives us a simple test: you will know them by their fruits (Matthew 7:16): humility, love and service.

Yesterday the Panchangam remembered St Benedict, who began his Rule with the word Listen. Let us listen today to the voice that says: Follow me. Let us leave one net at his feet, and let us serve without asking for a reward. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know what Jesus said to the fishermen? He said, Follow me! And they left their nets and boats right away, and went with him. They did not know everything about where they were going, but they loved Jesus and trusted him. Jesus calls you too. He does not call you to leave your family; he calls you to be kind, to pray, to help others and to listen to him. And St Paul tells us to serve people without asking for anything back, just like a good fisherman who shares his fish. This week, do one kind thing for someone without telling anyone, and say: Jesus, I want to follow you.
